title: StereoDetect: Detecting Stereotypes and Anti-stereotypes the Correct Way Using Social Psychological Underpinnings
benchmark_measurement: Detection of stereotypes and anti-stereotypes in religious contexts, using groups such as Muslims and Brahmins as targets.
findings: The paper's fine-tuned model (gemma-2-9b) on their new StereoDetect dataset achieved a high weighted F1-score of 0.9487 in the religion domain, effectively detecting stereotypes and anti-stereotypes. This demonstrates a significant improvement over baseline models and models trained on other datasets, which often misclassify nuanced religious statements, such as negated stereotypes (e.g., 'Not all Muslims are violent').
references: Andrea E. Abele and Bogdan Wojciszke. 2007. Agency and communion from the perspective of self versus others. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 93(5):751–763.
